newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Spanish-Bulgaria group to buy Bulgaria cement unit.
newsitem.headline: Spanish-Bulgaria group to buy Bulgaria cement unit.

text.p: The Spanish-Bulgarian investment consortium Marvex Ltd has been chosen as a buyer of 70 percent of Bulgaria's Devnya Ziment cement plant for $44.5 million, the consortium said in a statement on Thursday.
Marvex pledged to invest $209.5 million in the plant over the next five years, the statement faxed to Reuters said.
Marvex representative to Bulgaria Yasen Vasilev however said the consortium had not yet reached final agreement on the use of a nearby limestone quarry and the Black Sea port of Varna.
If the deal is not finalised before April 7 Marvex will lose its rights as a winner, he added.
Privatisation Agency officials were not immediately available for comment.

Vasilev said Spain's Moltiracion De Graneles held 80 percent of Marvex which had been specially set up for the privatisation deal. The other 20 percent is held by the Bulgarian private company ELVA, which is the distributor of Russian Lada cars in Bulgaria.
The Devnya Ziment plant, which exports 44 percent of its produce, had a turnover of 2.9 million levs in 1995.
Vasilev said Marvex planned to increase the plant's annual capacity to 4.5 million tonnes in the next five years from the current 1.8 million tonnes.

On Monday Bulgaria's interim government approved the sale of 51 percent of another cement plant, Beloizvorski Ziment, to Swiss building materials group Holderbank Financiere Glarus AG for $32.5 million.
